events.title: Imperial army captures Francis I at the Battle of Pavia
events.description: Charles V's troops routed the French outside Pavia, and King Francis I was taken prisoner. He was released in 1526 only after signing away claims in Italy and Burgundy.
events.html: Charles V's troops routed the French outside Pavia, and King Francis I was taken prisoner. He was released in 1526 only after signing away claims in Italy and Burgundy.

events.title: Pope Gregory XIII issues the bull reforming the calendar
events.description: The bull Inter gravissimas introduced the Gregorian calendar, dropping ten days that October to realign the calendar with the equinox. It is now the world's standard civil calendar.
events.html: The bull Inter gravissimas introduced the Gregorian calendar, dropping ten days that October to realign the calendar with the equinox. It is now the world's standard civil calendar.

events.title: Marbury v. Madison establishes judicial review
events.description: Chief Justice John Marshall ruled that the Supreme Court could strike down acts of Congress that conflicted with the Constitution. The decision became a cornerstone of American constitutional law.
events.html: Chief Justice John Marshall ruled that the Supreme Court could strike down acts of Congress that conflicted with the Constitution. The decision became a cornerstone of American constitutional law.

events.title: Plan of Iguala sets out Mexican independence
events.description: Agustín de Iturbide and Vicente Guerrero proclaimed a plan for an independent Mexican monarchy guaranteeing Catholicism and equality. Mexico's independence was declared that September.
events.html: Agustín de Iturbide and Vicente Guerrero proclaimed a plan for an independent Mexican monarchy guaranteeing Catholicism and equality. Mexico's independence was declared that September.

events.title: Hitler presents the Nazi Party's 25-point programme
events.description: At the Hofbräuhaus in Munich, Hitler read out the programme of the German Workers' Party, which renamed itself the National Socialist German Workers' Party (NSDAP) around this time.
events.html: At the Hofbräuhaus in Munich, Hitler read out the programme of the German Workers' Party, which renamed itself the National Socialist German Workers' Party (NSDAP) around this time.

events.title: Juan Perón elected President of Argentina
events.description: The former labour minister won the presidency with strong support from trade unions. With his wife Eva, he built the populist Peronist movement that still shapes Argentine politics.
events.html: The former labour minister won the presidency with strong support from trade unions. With his wife Eva, he built the populist Peronist movement that still shapes Argentine politics.
